0: ✦Your newborn spends most of the day (16–17 hours) sleeping.✦They want to feed every 2–3 hours, 8–12 times a day; breastfeed on demand.✦Losing 7–10% of birth weight in the first days is normal; most babies regain it within 10–14 days.✦Vision is blurry; they see best at 20–30 cm – just the distance to your face while feeding.✦At least 6 wet diapers a day is a good sign they're feeding enough.✦The umbilical cord stump falls off on its own in 1–3 weeks; keep it clean and dry.
1: ✦Your baby is one month old! They gain about 700–1,000 grams a month on average.✦On their tummy, they try to lift their head briefly.✦They react to sounds, recognise your voice and may calm down when they hear you.✦They love looking at faces; bold black-and-white patterns catch their eye.✦Supervised tummy time while awake strengthens the neck muscles.✦Gas pains are common now; burping and a gentle clockwise tummy massage can help.
2: ✦The first 'social smile' usually arrives this month – they smile at you on purpose!✦They start cooing.✦They follow moving objects with their eyes.✦On their tummy they can lift their head up to 45 degrees.✦They discover their hands and bring them to their mouth.✦Check the vaccination schedule with your doctor.
3: ✦They can hold their head steadier and longer.✦They reach for toys and try to grab them.✦They may start laughing.✦Night sleep begins to lengthen; a regular bedtime routine helps.✦Besides crying, they communicate with sounds and facial expressions.
4: ✦They may start rolling from back to side, or even onto their tummy.✦They hold toys, shake them and bring them to their mouth.✦With support, they try to sit.✦They laugh out loud and enjoy being tickled.✦Some babies have a '4-month sleep regression'; it's temporary.
5: ✦Their weight approaches double their birth weight.✦They can grab their feet and bring them to their mouth.✦They start responding to their name.✦They distinguish colours better.✦Solid foods usually start around 6 months; talk to your doctor about when to begin.
6: ✦Time to start solids! Introduce new foods one at a time, a few days apart.✦They can sit with support or briefly without it.✦First teeth may appear now; a teething ring can soothe.✦They may babble syllables like 'ba-ba' and 'ma-ma'.✦Shyness with strangers may begin.✦Don't give honey before 12 months.
7: ✦They sit without support and play with toys while sitting.✦They pass objects from one hand to the other.✦They're getting ready to crawl and may rock back and forth on hands and knees.✦They love peekaboo.✦Time to baby-proof your home: outlet covers, corner guards and stair gates.
8: ✦They may start crawling; every baby is different and some walk without ever crawling.✦They try to pull up to stand.✦They begin picking up small objects with thumb and finger – watch out for choking hazards!✦They may cry when you leave (separation anxiety); this is normal.
9: ✦They stand holding onto furniture and may cruise along the edges.✦They start to understand 'no'.✦They imitate gestures like waving and clapping.✦They try feeding themselves with finger foods.✦Two daytime naps are usually enough.
10: ✦They may stand alone for a moment.✦They understand simple requests like 'Give me the ball'.✦They love putting things into boxes and taking them out.✦They may say their first meaningful word.✦You can try drinking from a cup.
11: ✦They may take their first steps holding your hand or on their own.✦Interest in books grows; look at picture books together.✦They imitate tones of voice and 'chatter' as if talking.✦They can gradually join family meals (no added salt, small pieces).
12: ✦Happy birthday! Your baby is 1 year old 🎉✦Their weight is about three times their birth weight.✦They say a few words, know their name and understand simple requests.✦They're walking or close to it; starting to walk any time up to 18 months is normal.✦Book the 1-year check-up and vaccines with your doctor.✦Ask your doctor about switching to cow's milk and family meals.
